sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: Sometimes it can feel like the past is all we have,
sentences.zh: 有时，我们可能会觉得过去就是我们拥有的一切，

sentences.en: that memory is all that we are.
sentences.zh: 记忆就是我们的全部。

sentences.en: It's why we always return to what we did yesterday,
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们总是回到昨天做过的事情，

sentences.en: rehashing, revisiting,
sentences.zh: 反复咀嚼，重温，

sentences.en: that grandparent we should have visited,
sentences.zh: 那个我们本该探望的祖父母，

sentences.en: that summer that lasted forever.
sentences.zh: 那个仿佛永无止境的夏天。

sentences.en: Our personal reconstructions of the past,
sentences.zh: 我们对过去的个人重构，

sentences.en: edited, polished, and misremembered,
sentences.zh: 经过编辑、润色和错误的记忆，

sentences.en: are how we make meaning of ourselves in the present.
sentences.zh: 是我们如何在当下赋予自我意义的方式。

sentences.en: Today, two emotions that take us back in time.
sentences.zh: 今天，有两种情绪将我们带回过去。

sentences.en: Regret and nostalgia.
sentences.zh: 遗憾与怀旧。

sentences.en: The things we wish we could return to.
sentences.zh: 那些我们希望能重回的时刻。

sentences.en: It's like, where did all this time go?
sentences.zh: 就像是，这些时间都去哪儿了？

sentences.en: How do I already have a daughter that's graduated from high school?
sentences.zh: 我怎么会有一个已经高中毕业的女儿了？

sentences.en: And the things we wish we could change.
sentences.zh: 以及那些我们希望能改变的事情。

sentences.en: My biggest regret is not listening to my father
sentences.zh: 我最大的遗憾是没有听父亲

sentences.en: tell me about the mundane things that happened to him during the day.
sentences.zh: 跟我讲他白天发生的琐事。

sentences.en: How can we make these feelings work for us?
sentences.zh: 我们如何才能让这些感受为我们所用？

sentences.en: And what can we learn from them?
sentences.zh: 我们又能从中学习到什么？

sentences.en: Looking to our past to understand our present.
sentences.zh: 审视过去，以理解当下。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 本周《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Whether or not you believe in them,
sentences.zh: 无论你是否相信它们，

sentences.en: you probably have ghosts that haunt you.
sentences.zh: 你可能都有困扰着你的“鬼魂”。

sentences.en: Not something sinister,
sentences.zh: 不是什么邪恶的东西，

sentences.en: but something you just can't get rid of.
sentences.zh: 而是你无法摆脱的东西。

sentences.en: Hi there, Shankar and friends.
sentences.zh: 你好，尚卡尔和各位朋友。

sentences.en: Hello, Shankar.
sentences.zh: 你好，尚卡尔。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: I was calling about full blue eyes saying it.
sentences.zh: 我打电话是想说关于全蓝眼睛的事。

sentences.en: Regrets, I've had a few, so I won't list all of them.
sentences.zh: 遗憾，我有一些，所以我就不一一列举了。

sentences.en: My boyfriend of a year and I ended our relationship.
sentences.zh: 我和交往了一年的男友结束了关系。

sentences.en: It's just looking back and thinking that I could have done better, and I didn't.
sentences.zh: 回首往事，总觉得我本可以做得更好，但我没有。

sentences.en: All these things keep popping in my head of small things,
sentences.zh: 所有这些小事不断在脑海中浮现，

sentences.en: maybe something I should have said differently
sentences.zh: 也许有些话我本该换种方式说，

sentences.en: or something I should have done differently in a particular conversation
sentences.zh: 或者在某次谈话中，

sentences.en: or on a particular event.
sentences.zh: 或在某个特定事件中，我本该采取不同的做法。

sentences.en: It makes me cringe with regret and shame.
sentences.zh: 这让我因遗憾和羞愧而感到局促不安。

sentences.en: I had an affair.
sentences.zh: 我曾有过一段婚外情。

sentences.en: Everyone knows that it's not a secret, but it's a regret.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，这不是秘密，但确实是个遗憾。

sentences.en: My great regret is leaving Woodstock on Saturday morning.
sentences.zh: 我最大的遗憾是周六早上离开了伍德斯托克音乐节。

sentences.en: I was an evangelical Christian at the time,
sentences.zh: 当时我是一名福音派基督徒，

sentences.en: and I remember my friends asking me if I thought they were going to hell.
sentences.zh: 我记得朋友们问我，是否认为他们会下地狱。

sentences.en: And I told them that I thought they would go to hell if they did not become Christian.
sentences.zh: 我告诉他们，如果他们不成为基督徒，我想他们会下地狱。

sentences.en: And it's something that's bothered me for the last 10 years.
sentences.zh: 这件事在过去十年里一直困扰着我。

sentences.en: I am experiencing regrets on sometimes a minute-by-minute basis.
sentences.zh: 我有时甚至每分钟都在经历遗憾。

sentences.en: And it is the biggest regret of my life, honestly.
sentences.zh: 老实说，这是我一生中最大的遗憾。

sentences.en: That's it.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: I hope you have a great rest of your day.
sentences.zh: 祝你余下的一天过得愉快。

sentences.en: Bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: I don't know that I have a particular deep backstory about how I got into regret.
sentences.zh: 我不确定自己是否有一个关于如何陷入遗憾的特别深刻的背景故事。

sentences.en: I actually was just generally interested in social psychology.
sentences.zh: 其实我只是对社会心理学普遍感兴趣。

sentences.en: Amy Somerville is a psychology professor at Miami University of Ohio.
sentences.zh: 艾米·萨默维尔是俄亥俄州迈阿密大学的心理学教授。

sentences.en: She runs the Regret Lab,
sentences.zh: 她经营着“遗憾实验室”，

sentences.en: where she studies how people think about the choices they made
sentences.zh: 在那里她研究人们如何看待自己做出的选择，

sentences.en: and the choices they wish they'd made.
sentences.zh: 以及他们希望自己当初做出的选择。

sentences.en: One of the things that then drew me to regret from that
sentences.zh: 从那以后，吸引我研究遗憾的原因之一，

sentences.en: is the fact that regret is among our most common emotions.
sentences.zh: 是遗憾是我们最常见的情绪之一这一事实。

sentences.en: By some estimates, it's the second most common emotion mentioned in daily life
sentences.zh: 据估计，它是日常生活中提到的第二常见情绪，

sentences.en: and the most common negative emotion that we mention.
sentences.zh: 也是我们提到的最常见的负面情绪。

sentences.en: And so this is really a pervasive part of how people experience the world around them.
sentences.zh: 所以，这确实是人们体验周围世界的一种普遍方式。

sentences.en: And as I learned more, I really started to realize that regret is actually a very hopeful emotion.
sentences.zh: 随着了解的深入，我开始意识到遗憾实际上是一种非常有希望的情绪。

sentences.en: It's something that is helping us learn from our mistakes and do better in the future.
sentences.zh: 它能帮助我们从错误中吸取教训，并在未来做得更好。

sentences.en: So it's actually, I think, a really positive thing to get to study.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，能研究这个课题其实是一件非常积极的事情。

sentences.en: That's so interesting, Amy, because, of course, most of us think of regret as being a negative emotion
sentences.zh: 这太有趣了，艾米，因为当然，我们大多数人认为遗憾是一种负面情绪，

sentences.en: because it's painful.
sentences.zh: 因为它很痛苦。

sentences.en: But what you're saying makes me think about a listener who recently shared his story of regret with us.
sentences.zh: 但你所说的让我想起了一位最近与我们分享他遗憾故事的听众。

sentences.en: His name is Tom Bonsane.
sentences.zh: 他叫汤姆·邦萨恩。

sentences.en: Here's what he said.
sentences.zh: 以下是他所说的。

sentences.en: I'm wondering how common this is.
sentences.zh: 我想知道这种情况有多普遍。

sentences.en: Are people really good at taking what happened in the past and learning from it?
sentences.zh: 人们真的擅长从过去发生的事情中吸取教训吗？

sentences.en: What spells the difference between people who actually are behaving like Tom,
sentences.zh: 那些像汤姆一样，

sentences.en: taking a bad experience and saying, I'm actually going to use it,
sentences.zh: 能把糟糕的经历拿来利用的人，

sentences.en: and people who just sort of stay stuck in what that bad experience was and think about it over and over again?
sentences.zh: 与那些沉溺于糟糕经历中反复回想的人，区别究竟在哪里？

sentences.en: So I think the thing that really characterizes it is less about necessarily what kind of person you are,
sentences.zh: 我认为真正决定性的因素不在于你是什么样的人，

sentences.en: but rather the way that you're experiencing these thoughts.
sentences.zh: 而在于你体验这些想法的方式。

sentences.en: So there's something called rumination, which actually comes literally from bovine digestion,
sentences.zh: 有一种叫做“反刍”的东西，它实际上源自牛的消化过程，

sentences.en: the idea of how cows vomit back up things, chew them over, swallow them back down, and so on and so forth.
sentences.zh: 即牛把食物吐出来、咀嚼、咽下去，如此反复的过程。

sentences.en: And in terms of our thoughts, it's actually this idea of the same kind of process,
sentences.zh: 就我们的思想而言，它实际上是同样的过程，

sentences.en: that rumination is having thoughts sort of spring unwanted to mind,
sentences.zh: 反刍是指那些不请自来的想法涌入脑海，

sentences.en: and we're chewing them over without actually getting anything new out of them.
sentences.zh: 而我们却在反复咀嚼它们，却没有任何新的收获。

sentences.en: They're just repeatedly, intrusively becoming sort of part of our mental landscape.
sentences.zh: 它们只是反复地、侵入性地成为我们精神世界的一部分。

sentences.en: And what we found is that people who have ruminative regrets,
sentences.zh: 我们发现，那些有反刍式遗憾的人，

sentences.en: so that they're both having this regret but also having it be something that's intrusive and repeated,
sentences.zh: 即他们不仅有遗憾，而且这种遗憾是侵入性的、反复出现的，

sentences.en: tend to be people who are also experiencing the most negative outcomes,
sentences.zh: 往往也是经历最负面结果的人，

sentences.en: so are more likely to have clinical depression symptoms, anxiety symptoms, things like that.
sentences.zh: 所以他们更有可能出现临床抑郁症症状、焦虑症状等。

sentences.en: There are some regrets you can learn from, like Tom's story about trying out for the school play,
sentences.zh: 有些遗憾是可以从中学习的，比如汤姆关于参加学校戏剧试镜的故事，

sentences.en: but other regrets feel harder to overcome.
sentences.zh: 但其他遗憾则感觉更难克服。

sentences.en: I asked Amy Somerville about this, and I played her the story from Catherine Wiginton-Green,
sentences.zh: 我问了艾米·萨默维尔关于这个问题，并给她播放了凯瑟琳·威金顿-格林的故事，

sentences.en: a listener from Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 一位来自华盛顿特区的听众。

sentences.en: My main regret, what popped into my mind when I heard this on the podcast,
sentences.zh: 我主要的遗憾，当我听到播客里提到这个时，脑海中浮现的，

sentences.en: was regretting not stopping and seeing my estranged father.
sentences.zh: 就是后悔没有停下来去见我疏远的父亲。

sentences.en: He'd been estranged from our family for quite a while,
sentences.zh: 他与我们家疏远了很长一段时间，

sentences.en: and I had not seen him or spoken with him in a very long time, his choice.
sentences.zh: 我很久没有见过他，也没有和他说过话，这是他的选择。

sentences.en: And I was driving along Rock Creek Parkway with my boyfriend at the time, who is now my husband.
sentences.zh: 当时我和当时的男友（现在是我的丈夫）正开车沿着岩溪公园大道行驶。

sentences.en: And as we were driving up Rock Creek Parkway,
sentences.zh: 当我们开车经过岩溪公园大道时，

sentences.en: I looked to my right and saw him and the woman he married walking arm-in-arm.
sentences.zh: 我向右看，看到他和他的妻子挽着手走着。

sentences.en: And I saw him, and I told my husband to pull over immediately without thinking.
sentences.zh: 我看到了他，我不假思索地告诉丈夫立刻靠边停车。

sentences.en: And when we stopped the car, I started to unbuckle my seatbelt.
sentences.zh: 当我们停下车时，我开始解开安全带。

sentences.en: And then I stopped and paused for a moment and realized I had no idea what I was going to do
sentences.zh: 然后我停顿了一下，意识到我根本不知道自己要做什么，

sentences.en: or what I was going to say.
sentences.zh: 或者要说什么。

sentences.en: So I chickened out and buckled my seatbelt back and told my husband to keep driving.
sentences.zh: 所以我退缩了，重新系好安全带，告诉丈夫继续开车。

sentences.en: And then I burst into tears.
sentences.zh: 然后我泪如雨下。

sentences.en: And I realized that that was probably the last time I was going to see him,
sentences.zh: 我意识到那可能是我最后一次见到他，

sentences.en: and that was my only chance to talk to him again.
sentences.zh: 那是我再次与他交谈的唯一机会。

sentences.en: So I still regret that.
sentences.zh: 所以我至今仍为此感到遗憾。

sentences.en: There's something really poignant about that story, Amy,
sentences.zh: 那个故事真的很令人心酸，艾米，

sentences.en: because in this case, it doesn't sound as if the regret has the potential for learning.
sentences.zh: 因为在这种情况下，听起来这个遗憾似乎没有学习的潜力。

sentences.en: She says that she feels that the door was closed in terms of her ability to reconnect with her father.
sentences.zh: 她说她觉得与父亲重新建立联系的大门已经关闭了。

sentences.en: And she comes back to this memory over and over again
sentences.zh: 她一次又一次地回到这段记忆中，

sentences.en: and just remembers it as an opportunity that was loSt.
sentences.zh: 只是把它当作一个错失的机会来怀念。

sentences.en: Yeah, certainly in terms of the specific incidents that we regret,
sentences.zh: 是的，当然，就我们遗憾的具体事件而言，

sentences.en: they do seem to be most likely things where we had this opportunity in the moment,
sentences.zh: 它们确实最可能是那些我们在当时有机会，

sentences.en: but it's not something that we can go back and fix.
sentences.zh: 但却无法回头去修正的事情。

sentences.en: Because obviously, if we could just magically turn back and fix something,
sentences.zh: 因为很明显，如果我们能神奇地回头修正某事，

sentences.en: then most people would do that rather than continue to regret it.
sentences.zh: 那么大多数人都会那样做，而不是继续为此遗憾。

sentences.en: What I might say is that I would imagine that one of the reasons that this does rankle for this woman
sentences.zh: 我想说的是，我想这个女人之所以会感到痛苦，原因之一

sentences.en: is that it's about something that's important to her.
sentences.zh: 是因为这关乎她重视的事情。

sentences.en: It's about her family.
sentences.zh: 这关乎她的家庭。

sentences.en: And that perhaps this is something that she can carry forward
sentences.zh: 也许这正是她可以带入未来，

sentences.en: in terms of how she handles other relationships going forward.
sentences.zh: 用来处理其他关系的事情。

sentences.en: So I've heard people say that there are anecdotal reports that the things that people really regret
sentences.zh: 我听人说过，有轶事报道称，人们真正遗憾的事情，

sentences.en: are the things that they didn't do rather than the things that they did do.
sentences.zh: 往往是他们没做过的事，而不是他们做过的事。

sentences.en: Is that just anecdotal?
sentences.zh: 这仅仅是轶事吗？

sentences.en: Is that not actually true that people regret acts of omission more than acts of commission?
sentences.zh: 人们对不作为的遗憾比对作为的遗憾更多，这难道不是真的吗？

sentences.en: I would say there's some evidence for that.
sentences.zh: 我会说这有一些证据支持。

sentences.en: So one of the more famous studies on this thought about this in terms of something that happens over time.
sentences.zh: 关于这个想法，一项更著名的研究从时间推移的角度进行了思考。

sentences.en: And what those researchers argued is that we regret things we did a lot more in the moment.
sentences.zh: 那些研究人员认为，我们在当下对做过的事情感到遗憾更多。

sentences.en: So if you say something really stupid in a job interview,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你在面试中说了非常愚蠢的话，

sentences.en: you're going to walk out and have that hand-to-the-forehead feeling of,
sentences.zh: 你走出来时会有一种拍额头的懊恼感，

sentences.en: oh, why did I say that?
sentences.zh: 噢，我为什么要那样说？

sentences.en: That was such a terrible thing to have said in that moment.
sentences.zh: 在那一刻说出那样的话真是太糟糕了。

sentences.en: But in the long run, we tend to have things that are kind of incomplete goals stick around in our memory
sentences.zh: 但从长远来看，我们往往会有一些未完成的目标留在记忆中，

sentences.en: as kind of a mental to-do list, basically.
sentences.zh: 基本上就像一个精神待办事项清单。

sentences.en: And that as a result, our inactions wind up getting kind of added to that mental to-do liSt.
sentences.zh: 结果，我们的不作为最终被添加到了那个精神待办事项清单中。

sentences.en: So this may be something where if you ask me, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以这可能就是，如果你问我，你知道，

sentences.en: what could you have done instead of going to grad school?
sentences.zh: 除了读研你还能做什么？

sentences.en: I have this whole range of possibilities.
sentences.zh: 我有各种各样的可能性。

sentences.en: I could have been a doctor.
sentences.zh: 我可以成为一名医生。

sentences.en: I could have been a writer.
sentences.zh: 我可以成为一名作家。

sentences.en: I could have backpacked around Europe and found my passion.
sentences.zh: 我可以去欧洲背包旅行，找到我的热情所在。

sentences.en: And if you ask me, what are the things that you did yesterday that you could undo?
sentences.zh: 如果你问我，你昨天做过的事情里有什么可以撤销的？

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: I have a finite set of things I actually did in my life.
sentences.zh: 我一生中实际做过的事情是有限的。

sentences.en: And so over time, it may be that when we're trying to undo something bad that's happened to us,
sentences.zh: 所以随着时间的推移，当我们试图撤销发生在我们身上的坏事时，

sentences.en: it's easy to start imagining all of the things we might have done in the past
sentences.zh: 很容易开始想象我们在过去可能做过的所有事情，

sentences.en: because we have a lot more of those available to us than the things we actually did.
sentences.zh: 因为我们拥有的那些可能性比我们实际做过的事情要多得多。

sentences.en: There are times when we don't take responsibility for our actions.
sentences.zh: 有时我们确实不对自己的行为负责。

sentences.en: But at other times, we hold ourselves accountable for things that are outside our control.
sentences.zh: 但有时，我们也会为那些超出我们控制范围的事情承担责任。

sentences.en: James Cooper of Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, shared one of those stories with us.
sentences.zh: 来自宾夕法尼亚州匹兹堡的詹姆斯·库珀（James Cooper）与我们分享了其中一个故事。

sentences.en: My biggest regret is not listening to my father tell me about the mundane things that happened to him during the day
sentences.zh: 我最大的遗憾就是没有听父亲跟我讲他白天发生的那些琐事，

sentences.en: and instead just immediately asking for my mom when I called the house.
sentences.zh: 而是每次打电话回家时，总是直接找我妈妈。

sentences.en: Maybe when I talked to him, I could have picked up on some other signs too
sentences.zh: 也许当时如果我多和他聊聊，我也能察觉到一些其他的迹象，

sentences.en: and could have maybe prevented his suicide.
sentences.zh: 或许就能阻止他自杀。

sentences.en: You know, when I heard James' story, Amy, I wondered whether, you know, if he had spoken to his father more,
sentences.zh: 艾米，你知道吗，当我听到詹姆斯的故事时，我在想，如果他当时能多和父亲交流，

sentences.en: would he have actually picked up on his father's mental health?
sentences.zh: 他真的能察觉到父亲的心理健康问题吗？

sentences.en: And even if he had noticed, could he have actually stopped his father from committing suicide?
sentences.zh: 即便他注意到了，他真的能阻止父亲自杀吗？

sentences.en: And it seemed to me that in this case, James might have been taking on more responsibility than was actually warranted.

sentences.en: There are 279,000 children still in London.
sentences.zh: 许多人被炸毁了家园，看起来都很疲惫，但他们在这里感到安全，在地下一百英尺深处，他们的精神和毅力真是太棒了。

sentences.en: Many are bombed out of their homes, all look tired, but they feel safe here, a good hundred feet below ground, and their spirit and fortitude are simply grand.
sentences.zh: 这些人中的许多人都有关于严重的家庭动荡的怀旧记忆，他们的父亲被送去打仗，

sentences.en: And a lot of these people have these nostalgic memories about serious family upheaval, their dad being sent away to war,
sentences.zh: 他们因为伦敦遭到轰炸而被送往乡村。

sentences.en: them being sent to the countryside because London was being bombed.
sentences.zh: 你知道，家庭被拆散，一方面，你可以说这些是非常非常糟糕的创伤性记忆。

sentences.en: You know, families being separated and, you know, on the one hand, you could say these are really, really, you know, bad, traumatic memories.
sentences.zh: 但在人们为我们写下的几乎所有这些记忆中，他们都有这种胜利感、感激之情，

sentences.en: But in nearly all of these memories that people, you know, wrote about for us, they had this experience of triumph, of gratefulness,
sentences.zh: 对这些时光的感恩，因为一方面，它们很艰难。

sentences.en: of thankfulness for these times because on the one hand, they were tough.
sentences.zh: 但它们也剥离了生活中所有无意义的东西，提醒他们，你知道，

sentences.en: But they also sort of stripped away all the nonsense of life and reminded them, you know,
sentences.zh: 生命是多么珍贵，在家庭和有意义的联系方面，什么才是真正重要的。

sentences.en: how precious it is and what's really important in terms of their family and their meaningful connections.
sentences.zh: 所以我感觉怀旧中经常发生这种情况，你真的开始触及人们认为个人有价值和有意义的核心。

sentences.en: And so I feel like this often happens a lot in nostalgia is you really start to get at the core of what people find personally valuable and meaningful.
sentences.zh: 很多时候，这意味着痛苦、损失或艰辛。

sentences.en: And a lot of times that means suffering or loss or hardship.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我从你那里听到的是，在某种程度上，怀旧可能涉及对过去的某种改写。

sentences.en: So I think what I'm hearing you say in some ways is that nostalgia might involve some amount of rewriting of the paSt.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我们在某种程度上把自己看作这部电影的中心主角。

sentences.en: So, you know, we're seeing ourselves in some ways as the central protagonist of this movie.
sentences.zh: 我们看到了我们经历的挣扎和挑战，但也看到了胜利以及我们克服这些挑战的方式。

sentences.en: We're seeing, you know, the struggles and challenges we experienced, but also the triumphs and the ways we overcame those challenges.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，这些是，你知道，我内心作为记者的那部分会说这可能是对事情实际发生方式的错误记忆。

sentences.en: And in some ways, these are, you know, the journalist in me would say that this might be misremembering the way things actually happened.
sentences.zh: 但当然，心理学家会说这正是所有人类需要做的事情。

sentences.en: But, of course, a psychologist would say this is exactly what all human beings need to do.
sentences.zh: 我们需要记住我们所经历的事情，我们想告诉自己关于我们是怎样的人，以及我们是如何变成今天这样子的故事。

sentences.en: We need to remember the kinds of things that we went through and we want to tell ourselves stories about the kind of people we are and how we became this way.
sentences.zh: 我们需要记住我们所经历的事情，我们想告诉自己关于我们是怎样的人，以及我们是如何变成今天这样子的故事。

sentences.en: And some rewriting of history, some recollection of the facts that suits our image of who we are today is what produces these nostalgic images.
sentences.zh: 而对历史进行某种重写，对事实进行某种符合我们今日自我形象的回忆，正是这些怀旧意象产生的原因。

sentences.en: To me, I see it's almost like making a movie.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这就像是在制作一部电影。

sentences.en: You have all these memories that represent raw footage, right, of all the filming that you've done.
sentences.zh: 你拥有所有代表原始素材的记忆，对吧，也就是你所拍摄的所有镜头。

sentences.en: And, of course, anyone who's seen them who's made a movie or watched a movie knows you don't go watch hundreds of hours of raw footage.
sentences.zh: 当然，任何看过电影或制作过电影的人都知道，你不会去观看数百小时的原始素材。

sentences.en: That would be a horrible movie, right?
sentences.zh: 那会是一部糟糕透顶的电影，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, you have an editing process, a process where the director and editors and people involved with the film will, you know,
sentences.zh: 嗯，你有一个剪辑过程，在这个过程中，导演、剪辑师和参与电影制作的人员会，你知道，

sentences.en: will sort of shape and edit the movie in a way that tells the story that they want to tell
sentences.zh: 会以某种方式塑造和剪辑电影，从而讲述他们想要讲述的故事，

sentences.en: or that features the most central themes in a narrative in a meaningful way.
sentences.zh: 或者以一种有意义的方式突出叙事中最核心的主题。

sentences.en: And, you know, we do that to some extent with our autobiographical memories as well.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我们在某种程度上也会用我们的自传式记忆来做这件事。

sentences.en: So it's not the case that we're necessarily completely fabricating memories so much as we're selecting and kind of weaving these different memories into a meaningful self-narrative
sentences.zh: 所以，这并不一定意味着我们完全在编造记忆，更多的是我们在选择并将这些不同的记忆编织成一种有意义的自我叙事，

sentences.en: that helps us make some sense of our lives and our connection to others.
sentences.zh: 这有助于我们理解自己的生活以及与他人的联系。

sentences.en: Now, this doesn't mean it can't go wrong or that people don't have, you know, false memories.
sentences.zh: 当然，这并不意味着它不会出错，或者人们不会有，你知道，虚假记忆。

sentences.en: But I think a decent portion of this is healthy recollection that's not necessarily false but does involve a certain level of, you know, massaging the raw footage, so to speak.
sentences.zh: 但我认为其中很大一部分是健康的记忆，它们不一定是虚假的，但确实涉及一定程度的，你知道，对原始素材的“润色”，可以这么说。

sentences.en: When we come back, I'm going to talk to Clay about the effects of nostalgia.
sentences.zh: 回来后，我将与克莱讨论怀旧的影响。

sentences.en: Is it a force for good or a force for bad?
sentences.zh: 它是一种向善的力量，还是一种向恶的力量？

sentences.en: And I'm going to ask him about one of the most nostalgia-invoking presidential campaigns in recent history.
sentences.zh: 我还要问他关于近代史上最能唤起怀旧之情的总统竞选活动之一。

sentences.en: We will make America great again.
sentences.zh: 我们要让美国再次伟大。

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请继续收听。

sentences.en: Welcome back to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: Why are we so mesmerized by the touchstones of our youth?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们如此迷恋青春时代的那些标志性事物？

sentences.en: Just look at all the outpouring of glee around reboots of TV shows like The X-Files.
sentences.zh: 看看围绕《X档案》这类电视剧重启所引发的狂喜就知道了。

sentences.en: I think those kids have been abducted.
sentences.zh: 我想那些孩子被绑架了。

sentences.en: By who?
sentences.zh: 被谁？

sentences.en: By what?
sentences.zh: 被什么？

sentences.en: Twin Peaks.
sentences.zh: 《双峰》。

sentences.en: This is a damn fine cup of coffee.
sentences.zh: 这咖啡真是好喝极了。

sentences.en: And Queer Eye.
sentences.zh: 还有《粉雄救兵》。

sentences.en: You spray, delay, and walk away.
sentences.zh: 喷一喷，缓一缓，然后走开。

sentences.en: Today we're thinking about the power of nostalgia and why the act of reminiscing can help us search for meaning
sentences.zh: 今天我们正在思考怀旧的力量，以及为什么回忆的行为可以帮助我们寻找意义，

sentences.en: and rewrite the stories of our lives.
sentences.zh: 并重写我们人生的故事。

sentences.en: Believe it or not, tapping into treasured memories hasn't always been considered a great idea.
sentences.zh: 信不信由你，挖掘珍贵的记忆并不总是被认为是一个好主意。

sentences.en: When Johannes Hoffer came up with the word nostalgia more than 300 years ago,
sentences.zh: 当约翰内斯·霍弗在300多年前提出“怀旧”这个词时，

sentences.en: he thought of it as a brain disease essentially caused by demons.
sentences.zh: 他认为这本质上是一种由恶魔引起的大脑疾病。

sentences.en: More recently, psychology professor Claire Rutledge has found nostalgia may actually be good for us.
sentences.zh: 最近，心理学教授克莱尔·拉特利奇发现，怀旧实际上可能对我们有益。

sentences.en: Yes, if you look within what we would refer to as normal populations,
sentences.zh: 是的，如果你观察我们所说的正常人群，

sentences.en: so these are research participants that don't have any particular vulnerability that might distinguish the way they recollect on the past,
sentences.zh: 也就是那些没有任何特殊脆弱性、可能导致他们回忆过去方式有所不同的研究参与者，

sentences.en: what you find is nostalgia seems to be generally a net positive experience that has a whole host of psychological benefits.
sentences.zh: 你会发现怀旧通常是一种净正向的体验，具有一系列心理益处。

sentences.en: I suppose it's possible for people to argue, you know, if you spend excessive amounts of time ruminating about the past
sentences.zh: 我想人们可能会争辩说，你知道，如果你花过多的时间沉思过去，

sentences.en: and living in the past, this could also be bad for you.
sentences.zh: 并活在过去，这可能对你也有害。

sentences.en: I mean, isn't it possible that people who are spending huge amounts of time in the past,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，难道那些花大量时间沉浸在过去的人，

sentences.en: in some ways I think your research and other people's research is suggesting,
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，我认为你的研究和其他人的研究都在暗示，

sentences.en: if distress causes people to become nostalgic, then people who are excessively nostalgic,
sentences.zh: 如果痛苦导致人们变得怀旧，那么那些过度怀旧的人，

sentences.en: could they not be people who are experiencing high levels of distress?
sentences.zh: 难道不可能是正在经历高度痛苦的人吗？

sentences.en: Yes, I mean, in fact, we find that characteristics like loneliness,
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，事实上，我们发现像孤独这样的特征，

sentences.en: so loneliness which we all experience from time to time, but it's also a trait,
sentences.zh: 也就是我们每个人都会时不时经历的孤独，但它也是一种特质，

sentences.en: like some people tend to be more lonely than others,
sentences.zh: 就像有些人往往比其他人更孤独一样，

sentences.en: are associated with nostalgia as is neuroticism.
sentences.zh: 与怀旧有关，神经质也是如此。

sentences.en: So these negative emotional traits tend to be associated with nostalgia,
sentences.zh: 所以这些负面情绪特质往往与怀旧有关，

sentences.en: but there's also a reason to suspect that these experiences of nostalgia are helping people restore some sense of psychological well-being
sentences.zh: 但也有理由怀疑，这些怀旧体验正在帮助人们恢复某种心理健康感，

sentences.en: while people are experiencing these emotions.
sentences.zh: 当人们正在经历这些情绪时。

sentences.en: Besides being an expert on nostalgia, Clay,
sentences.zh: 克莱，除了是怀旧方面的专家，

sentences.en: you've spent a lot of time advocating for greater ideological diversity in the social sciences.
sentences.zh: 你还花了很多时间倡导社会科学中更大的意识形态多样性。

sentences.en: You've made the case that more conservative voices need to be part of the conversation.
sentences.zh: 你提出了更保守的声音需要参与对话的观点。

sentences.en: I'd like to try and connect these two parts of your life,
sentences.zh: 我想试着把你生活中的这两个部分联系起来，

sentences.en: the researcher who studies nostalgia on the one hand and the person who's interested in conservative thought on the other hand,
sentences.zh: 一方面是研究怀旧的研究者，另一方面是对保守思想感兴趣的人，

sentences.en: and I want to do it by talking about the 2016 presidential campaign of Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 我想通过谈论唐纳德·特朗普2016年的总统竞选来做到这一点。

sentences.en: Lots of presidential campaigns talk about the future.
sentences.zh: 许多总统竞选活动都在谈论未来。

sentences.en: They talk about how change is coming, about hope for the future,
sentences.zh: 他们谈论变革即将到来，谈论对未来的希望，

sentences.en: but Donald Trump very specifically turned his attention toward the paSt.
sentences.zh: 但唐纳德·特朗普非常明确地将注意力转向了过去。

sentences.en: He invoked a sense of nostalgia among followers,
sentences.zh: 他在追随者中唤起了一种怀旧感，

sentences.en: and he communicated the idea that America had seen brighter days,
sentences.zh: 他传达了美国曾经有过更美好时光的理念，

sentences.en: and both he and his followers felt that they wanted to make America great again.
sentences.zh: 他和他的追随者都觉得他们想让美国再次伟大。

sentences.en: I'm wondering whether the science of nostalgia has any insights into the appeal of Donald Trump
sentences.zh: 我想知道怀旧科学是否对唐纳德·特朗普的吸引力，

sentences.en: and the success of his presidential campaign.
sentences.zh: 以及他总统竞选的成功有任何见解。

sentences.en: Well, I think one thing that's important to distinguish
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为有一点很重要，那就是要区分，

sentences.en: is the difference between what we might call personal nostalgia and historical or what some people call collective nostalgia.
sentences.zh: 我们所说的个人怀旧与历史怀旧（有些人称之为集体怀旧）之间的区别。

sentences.en: Now, a lot of the work that I've done or nearly all the work I've done
sentences.zh: 现在，我所做的大量工作，或者说我所做的几乎所有工作，

sentences.en: and pretty much everything we've talked about thus far is about this idea of personal nostalgia,
sentences.zh: 以及到目前为止我们谈论的几乎所有内容，都是关于这种个人怀旧的理念，

sentences.en: which is us revisiting memories from our own past, right,
sentences.zh: 也就是我们重温自己过去记忆的过程，对吧，

sentences.en: our own childhood or youth or whenever.
sentences.zh: 我们自己的童年、青年时期或其他任何时候。

sentences.en: Like, these are our personal memories.
sentences.zh: 比如，这些是我们个人的记忆。

sentences.en: And that seems to be distinct from this more historical nostalgia,
sentences.zh: 这似乎与这种更具历史性的怀旧不同，

sentences.en: which you can imagine having nostalgic feelings for a period of time
sentences.zh: 你可以想象对一个时期产生怀旧之情，

sentences.en: or for an idea that you never actually had any direct contact with.
sentences.zh: 或者对一个你从未真正直接接触过的想法产生怀旧之情。

sentences.en: So there are people, you know, to step outside of politics for just a second,
sentences.zh: 所以有些人，你知道，暂时跳出政治话题，

sentences.en: there are people that have nostalgia for the 1920s.
sentences.zh: 有些人对20世纪20年代有怀旧之情。

sentences.en: They just think everything about from the architecture to the fashion,
sentences.zh: 他们只是认为从建筑到时尚的一切，

sentences.en: that everything's great, and they never, you know, they never lived in that time.
sentences.zh: 一切都很棒，而他们从未，你知道，他们从未生活在那个时代。

sentences.en: And so they can't really trace it to a personal or autobiographical experience.
sentences.zh: 所以他们无法真正将其追溯到个人的或自传式的经历。

sentences.en: And so I think that's important.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这一点很重要。

sentences.en: What Trump seems to have done either by design or by just stumbling onto it
sentences.zh: 特朗普似乎所做的，无论是刻意为之还是偶然碰巧，

sentences.en: was really latch onto this idea of historic nostalgia,
sentences.zh: 确实是抓住了这种历史怀旧的理念，

sentences.en: that there's some kind of collective feeling of nostalgia
sentences.zh: 即存在某种集体怀旧感，

sentences.en: that's beyond any individual experience that is about a time that perhaps was,
sentences.zh: 这种感觉超越了任何个人经历，是关于一个也许，

sentences.en: at least for some, they, you know, in their mind, imagine that was better.
sentences.zh: 至少对某些人来说，在他们心中，想象中曾经更美好的时代。

sentences.en: Now, of course, that doesn't mean that it was.
sentences.zh: 当然，这并不意味着它真的更美好。

sentences.en: What matters is that, you know, he sold the idea.
sentences.zh: 重要的是，你知道，他兜售了这个理念。

sentences.en: I have to say, when I was young in high school and college,
sentences.zh: 我必须说，当我年轻在高中和大学时，

sentences.en: everybody used to say, we never lost to war.
sentences.zh: 每个人都常说，我们从未输过战争。

sentences.en: We never lost to war.
sentences.zh: 我们从未输过战争。

sentences.en: You know what I hate?
sentences.zh: 你知道我讨厌什么吗？

sentences.en: There's a guy, totally disruptive, throwing punches.
sentences.zh: 有个家伙，完全是个捣乱分子，到处挥拳头。

sentences.en: We're not allowed to punch back anymore.
sentences.zh: 我们不再被允许反击了。

sentences.en: I love the old days.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢过去的日子。

sentences.en: You know what they used to do to guys like that when they were in a place like this?
sentences.zh: 你知道他们过去是怎么对待像那样的人的吗，当他们在像这样的地方时？

sentences.en: They'd be carried out on a stretcher, folks.
sentences.zh: 他们会被担架抬出去，伙计们。

sentences.en: You know, I'd also add that it's not specific to Trump,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我还要补充一点，这并非特朗普所特有，

sentences.en: though that's, you know, clearly the most recent example from our culture.
sentences.zh: 尽管这显然是我们文化中最近的例子。

sentences.en: But there's actually, you know, people that have looked into Soviet-era nostalgia,
sentences.zh: 但实际上，你知道，有人研究过苏联时代的怀旧，

sentences.en: that there are people in Eastern Europe and Russia that have nostalgia for the Soviet Union,
sentences.zh: 东欧和俄罗斯有人对苏联怀有怀旧之情，

sentences.en: even if they were, you know, too young to really fully understand what was going on that time.
sentences.zh: 即使他们，你知道，当时太年轻，无法完全理解那时发生了什么。

sentences.en: So this idea of historical nostalgia is definitely its own kind of beaSt.
sentences.zh: 所以这种历史怀旧的理念绝对是另一种“野兽”。

sentences.en: And I don't feel like, as far as the science of it, we really have a full handle on it yet.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得，就其科学性而言，我们还没有完全掌握它。

sentences.en: So obviously it's much harder to study collective nostalgia and shared nostalgia
sentences.zh: 所以很明显，研究集体怀旧和共享怀旧要比研究个人怀旧困难得多，

sentences.en: than it is to study individual nostalgia.
sentences.zh: 因为研究个人怀旧更容易。

sentences.en: You know, you can't bring countries into your lab and evaluate, you know, millions of people.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你不能把国家带进你的实验室，去评估，你知道，数百万的人。

sentences.en: But is it possible that at a collective level,
sentences.zh: 但有没有可能在集体层面上，

sentences.en: nostalgia performs the same function that it does at an individual level?
sentences.zh: 怀旧发挥着与在个人层面上相同的功能？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's a reasonable hypothesis.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这是一个合理的假设。

sentences.en: For example, there are, you know, that people have noted that at, like at the time of the, you know,
sentences.zh: 例如，有人注意到，在，比如在，你知道，

sentences.en: following the economic recession in the United States,
sentences.zh: 美国经济衰退之后，

sentences.en: you saw this peak kind of interest in nostalgia products,
sentences.zh: 你看到了对怀旧产品兴趣的这种高峰，

sentences.en: whether it was, you know, reboots of movies or, you know,
sentences.zh: 无论是，你知道，电影的重启，还是，你知道，

sentences.en: or those types of, you know, those types of cultural consumption products.
sentences.zh: 或者那些类型的，你知道，那些类型的文化消费产品。

sentences.en: Now, these aren't experiments, of course, and they're not even really, you know, scientific.
sentences.zh: 当然，这些不是实验，甚至也不是真正的，你知道，科学的。

sentences.en: They're in the sense that no one tried to systematically study this.
sentences.zh: 它们之所以不是，是因为没有人试图系统地研究这一点。

sentences.en: But there was, you know, some acknowledgement that it seems like in times of collective upheaval,
sentences.zh: 但确实有，你知道，一些承认，似乎在集体动荡时期，

sentences.en: just like times of personal upheaval, people seem to turn more to nostalgic feelings.
sentences.zh: 就像个人动荡时期一样，人们似乎更多地转向怀旧情绪。

sentences.en: So I think that, you know, that's certainly a reasonable possibility.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，你知道，这当然是一个合理的可能性。

sentences.en: We talked earlier in our conversations about how recollections of our past might not necessarily be fabrications,
sentences.zh: 我们在之前的谈话中讨论过，我们对过去的记忆可能不一定是编造的，

sentences.en: but they are selective edits in some ways of our history.
sentences.zh: 但它们在某种程度上是我们历史的选择性编辑。

sentences.en: So, you know, you have that photograph on your desk of you standing with your family in front of the London mural.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，你的桌子上放着那张你和家人站在伦敦壁画前的照片。

sentences.en: And, you know, you remember the good parts of that history and your story.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，你记得那段历史和你故事中美好的部分。

sentences.en: You know, you don't necessarily remember that maybe that morning,
sentences.zh: 你知道，你不一定会记得那天早上，

sentences.en: maybe you weren't the best dad that you could have been.
sentences.zh: 也许你并不是你所能做到的最好的父亲。

sentences.en: Maybe you were impatient or you were short-tempered.
sentences.zh: 也许你当时不耐烦或脾气暴躁。

sentences.en: I mean, you don't remember that part of it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你不记得那部分了。

sentences.en: You remember just the fact that you were facing a challenge with your family and, you know,
sentences.zh: 你只记得你和家人面临挑战的事实，而且，你知道，

sentences.en: you were on a big adventure.
sentences.zh: 你们正在进行一场大冒险。

sentences.en: And I'm wondering, is the same thing possibly true at a collective level as well,
sentences.zh: 我想知道，同样的事情是否也可能发生在集体层面上，

sentences.en: which is, you know, we have these nostalgic memories,
sentences.zh: 也就是，你知道，我们有这些怀旧的记忆，

sentences.en: but is it possible there's an element of them that really is insidious,
sentences.zh: 但有没有可能它们中确实存在一种阴险的成分，

sentences.en: especially at a cultural level?
sentences.zh: 特别是在文化层面上？

sentences.en: When you see the debate over Confederate memorials, for example,
sentences.zh: 当你看到关于邦联纪念碑的辩论时，例如，

sentences.en: and the nostalgia that people feel over Confederate memorials,
sentences.zh: 以及人们对邦联纪念碑所感受到的怀旧之情，

sentences.en: many people will say this is tradition and this is nostalgia.
sentences.zh: 许多人会说这是传统，这是怀旧。

sentences.en: And there are equally many people on the other side who say you're remembering a history
sentences.zh: 而另一方也有同样多的人说，你记住的是一段历史，

sentences.en: that essentially has whitewashed, you know, the issue of slavery
sentences.zh: 它本质上已经粉饰了，你知道，奴隶制的问题，

sentences.en: or the issue of race relationships from that memory
sentences.zh: 或者那段记忆中种族关系的问题，

sentences.en: and replaced it with this relatively grand and benign idea of tradition.
sentences.zh: 并用这种相对宏大且良性的传统理念取而代之。

sentences.en: How would you respond to that?
sentences.zh: 你会如何回应这一点？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's a fair point, even with the example of personal nostalgia.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这是一个公平的观点，即使是以个人怀旧为例。

sentences.en: Nostalgia can be a source of inspiration and a stabilizing force as well,
sentences.zh: 怀旧也可以成为灵感的源泉和一种稳定的力量，

sentences.en: but you shouldn't let it blind you or it shouldn't be the only dimension
sentences.zh: 但你不应该让它蒙蔽你的双眼，或者它不应该成为你思考这些问题的唯一维度，

sentences.en: through which you think about these issues because you're absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 因为你是完全正确的。

sentences.en: It's part of our psychological immune system to, you know,
sentences.zh: 这是我们心理免疫系统的一部分，你知道，

sentences.en: more easily forget the negative features of the past,
sentences.zh: 更容易忘记过去的负面特征，

sentences.en: either through this sort of revisionist process that you mentioned
sentences.zh: 无论是通过你提到的这种修正主义过程，

sentences.en: or even through just natural recollection.
sentences.zh: 还是仅仅通过自然的回忆。

sentences.en: I mean, a lot of negative memories fade from, you know,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，很多负面记忆会从我们的意识中淡去，你知道的，

sentences.en: our awareness faster than positive memories,
sentences.zh: 比正面记忆淡去得更快，

sentences.en: and this seems to be adaptive for us personally moving forward in life,
sentences.zh: 这似乎对我们个人在生活中继续前行具有适应性，

sentences.en: but it also biases us towards, you know, not necessarily doing a good job
sentences.zh: 但它也让我们产生了一种偏见，你知道，未必能很好地

sentences.en: of thinking about the complexities of the whole picture
sentences.zh: 去思考全局的复杂性，

sentences.en: and thinking about other people's experiences,
sentences.zh: 以及去思考他人的经历，

sentences.en: which may be, giving the Confederate example, vastly different than our own.
sentences.zh: 以邦联的例子来说，这些经历可能与我们自己的截然不同。

sentences.en: And so I do think that, though, nostalgia certainly has a number of positive benefits
sentences.zh: 所以我确实认为，虽然怀旧肯定有很多积极的好处，

sentences.en: that we shouldn't let ourselves be intoxicated by nostalgia
sentences.zh: 但我们不应该让自己沉溺于怀旧之中，

sentences.en: because there are some real dangers associated with that.
sentences.zh: 因为这其中确实存在一些真正的危险。

sentences.en: Clay and I wrapped up our conversation by talking about what he said
sentences.zh: 我和克莱（Clay）在谈话结束时，聊到了他所说的

sentences.en: was the most surprising finding about nostalgia.
sentences.zh: 关于怀旧最令人惊讶的发现。

sentences.en: Nostalgia seems to actually orient people towards the future.
sentences.zh: 怀旧似乎实际上能让人们面向未来。

sentences.en: And so part of what seems to be going on is you experience some kind of distress,
sentences.zh: 所以，其中发生的一部分情况是，当你经历某种痛苦时，

sentences.en: which kind of makes you shrink a little bit from pursuing goals and from the future.
sentences.zh: 这会让你在追求目标和面对未来时产生一点退缩。

sentences.en: Like, it does kick you into more of this defensive mode.
sentences.zh: 就像它确实会让你进入这种防御模式一样。

sentences.en: And then you bring to mind these nostalgic experiences that they don't only make you feel good.
sentences.zh: 然后你回想起这些怀旧的经历，它们不仅让你感觉良好，

sentences.en: We now have evidence that they actually make you feel optimistic and hopeful about the future.
sentences.zh: 我们现在有证据表明，它们实际上让你对未来感到乐观和充满希望。

sentences.en: And so that, in turn, seems to mobilize people, particularly in the social domain.
sentences.zh: 因此，这反过来似乎能调动人们的积极性，特别是在社交领域。

sentences.en: And now we have, you know, a number of studies that show this,
sentences.zh: 现在我们有，你知道，许多研究都证明了这一点，

sentences.en: both in terms of people reporting that they're more optimistic about the future, more inspired,
sentences.zh: 既体现在人们报告说他们对未来更乐观、更有灵感，

sentences.en: but also behaviorally, too, in terms of people actually going out and wanting to interact with and meet people
sentences.zh: 也体现在行为上，即人们在怀旧之后，

sentences.en: after they've engaged in nostalgia.
sentences.zh: 确实会走出去，想要与人互动和结识他人。

sentences.en: So at one level, actually, this is surprising.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种程度上说，这确实令人惊讶。

sentences.en: But as you're talking just now, I realize this also makes perfect sense.
sentences.zh: 但正如你刚才所说，我意识到这也完全讲得通。

sentences.en: I mean, people are nostalgic in every culture.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在每种文化中，人们都会怀旧。

sentences.en: And as far as we can tell, have always, you know, all historical reports suggest that nostalgia is very widespread.
sentences.zh: 据我们所知，一直以来，你知道，所有的历史记录都表明怀旧是非常普遍的。

sentences.en: And when you see something that's as widespread as nostalgia seems to be, it's reasonable to draw the conclusion
sentences.zh: 当你看到像怀旧这样普遍的现象时，得出这样的结论是合理的：

sentences.en: this is performing some kind of adaptive function and not just helping people feel better,
sentences.zh: 它发挥着某种适应性功能，不仅仅是帮助人们感觉更好，

sentences.en: but in actually being able to function better.
sentences.zh: 而且实际上能让人更好地发挥功能。

sentences.en: Nostalgia has had this, historically had this stigma, as we talked about it.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所谈到的，怀旧在历史上一直带有这种污名。

sentences.en: It started out very much as being considered a disease.
sentences.zh: 它最初在很大程度上被认为是一种疾病。

sentences.en: And people even today, a lot of people will say, well, I'm not nostalgic because I think about the future.
sentences.zh: 即使在今天，很多人也会说，嗯，我不怀旧，因为我考虑的是未来。

sentences.en: You know, I'm not the type of person that likes to fixate or get stuck in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我不是那种喜欢固步自封或沉溺于过去的人。

sentences.en: And I think what they're missing when they say that is there is a big element of nostalgia
sentences.zh: 我认为他们这样说时忽略了一点，那就是怀旧中有一个重要的元素，

sentences.en: that isn't about us retreating to the paSt.
sentences.zh: 它不是关于我们退回到过去。

sentences.en: It's about us pulling the past forward to the present and using it to mobilize us,
sentences.zh: 而是关于我们将过去拉向现在，并利用它来激励我们，

sentences.en: to energize us, to take on new challenges and opportunities.
sentences.zh: 让我们充满活力，去迎接新的挑战和机遇。
